# Synthesized Code Review — PR #240
**Branch:** feat/issue-230-migrate-reviewer-family
**Synthesis Date:** 2026-04-29
**Review Type:** Multi-model synthesis (Claude + Qwen + GLM)
**Commit at Review:** a08bf57 feat(agents): migrate Reviewer family to OpenCode (#230)

> **Timing note:** The Claude raw report was written against the pre-fix commit. Two subsequent fixes were applied before the Qwen and GLM reports were written: (1) orchestrator allow-list updated from parenthetical forms (`"Reviewer (Kimi)"`) to filename-derived forms (`"Reviewer Kimi"`); (2) YAML indentation corrected in `orchestrator-v3.md`. Claude findings that map to those fixes are classified **Already Fixed** and excluded from open finding counts.

---

## Synthesis Overview

This PR migrates five reviewer-family agents from the legacy `.github/agents-openrouter/` format into `.opencode/agents/`, covering three model-specific reviewer sub-agents (Kimi, Qwen, GLM), the Synthesizing Reviewer, and the standalone PR Reviewer. The orchestrator allow-list and Step 7 dispatch instructions are updated in tandem. All three reviewers found the overall structure sound — correct `mode: subagent` declarations, appropriate `permission.task.deny` on the synthesizer (honouring the PR #70 freeze-prevention constraint), well-formed bash allow-lists, and body text that correctly references existing shared process files. The blocking name-mismatch defect identified by Claude was resolved before the Qwen and GLM reviews, and both post-fix reviewers confirmed alignment. The remaining open findings are all Suggestion-level documentation nits, with one Warning-level testing observation from Qwen.

**Model Agreement Score:** 7/10 — Broad agreement that the PR is structurally correct post-fix. Minor divergence on (a) whether the unverified runtime dispatch naming warrants a merge hold, and (b) the severity of documentation inaccuracy in `pr-reviewer.md`. Timing asymmetry (one pre-fix, two post-fix reports) slightly reduces confidence in cross-report comparisons.

## Individual Report Summaries

| Model  | Overall Assessment                                                                 | Unique Focus Areas                                                          | Critical Count | Warning Count |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| Claude | Not ready to merge (pre-fix); blocking name-mismatch in orchestrator allow-list   | Filename-derivation analysis; pr-reviewer description accuracy; {N} variable | 1 (fixed)      | 1 (partial)   |
| Qwen   | Close to merge; hold for one runtime smoke test                                   | Runtime verification gap; three naming surfaces on pr-reviewer              | 0              | 1             |
| GLM    | Approved; no open findings                                                        | Confirmed synthesizer task:deny correctness; bash constraint coverage        | 0              | 0             |

**Claude** performed the most detailed static analysis, identifying the root-cause name-mismatch by tracing OpenCode's filename-derivation rule and its interaction with the orchestrator allow-list. The two fixes applied between reviews resolved the Critical finding entirely.

**Qwen** reviewed the post-fix state, confirmed the structural fix is correct, and shifted focus to the verification gap: no smoke-test evidence exists that the renamed dispatch paths were exercised at runtime before merge.

**GLM** also reviewed post-fix, explicitly confirmed the synthesizer's `task: deny` constraint honours the PR #70 freeze-prevention resolution, and found no open issues. Its sole suggestion (identical body text across reviewer files) was offered as an out-of-scope follow-up.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

None — after accounting for already-fixed findings, no finding was independently raised by all three models.

---

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-S-01] pr-reviewer.md description inaccuracy and naming surface split
Severity: Suggestion (downgraded from Claude's Warning — see note below)
Category: Documentation
File: .opencode/agents/pr-reviewer.md
Lines: 2 (frontmatter description), 30 (body)
Detail: Two related but distinct issues:

  (a) Description inaccuracy: Both the frontmatter `description:` field and the body state
      "You are not part of the Orchestrator workflow." This is incorrect — `pr-reviewer.md`
      IS listed in orchestrator-v3.md's `permission.task.allow` (line 45: "Pr Reviewer")
      and CAN be dispatched by the Orchestrator for ad-hoc GitHub PR reviews. The intended
      meaning is that the PR Reviewer is not used in the Step 7 Synthesized Local Review
      cycle (that cycle uses the three model-specific sub-agents and the Synthesizing
      Reviewer). An agent or human reading this description may incorrectly infer the PR
      Reviewer is never Orchestrator-dispatched.

  (b) Three naming surfaces: The agent is referenced in three different forms — the manual
      invocation slug (`@pr-reviewer`), the OpenCode-derived task name used in the
      orchestrator allow-list ("Pr Reviewer"), and the branding used in the body prose and
      report template ("PR Reviewer"). This is not functionally broken, but makes dispatch
      debugging harder — especially in a PR whose core behaviour depends on filename-derived
      naming conventions.

  Note on downgrade: Claude's W-01 (Warning) was partly predicated on the now-fixed
  "Pr Reviewer" allow-list mismatch. The remaining open issues are documentation nits.
  Qwen also raised this as Suggestion severity. GLM did not raise it. Consensus: Suggestion.

Models: Claude ✓ Qwen ✓ GLM ✗
Dissenting view: GLM found no issue with pr-reviewer.md and approved the file as-is.
Suggestion:
  (a) Revise description in both frontmatter and body to: "You are invoked directly by the
      user or the Orchestrator for ad-hoc GitHub PR reviews. You are not part of the
      Step 7 Synthesized Local Review cycle — that cycle uses the three model-specific
      reviewer sub-agents and the Synthesizing Reviewer."
  (b) Consider adding a one-line note near the top of the body: "Invocation: @pr-reviewer
      (direct) or via Orchestrator as 'Pr Reviewer'." This makes all three naming surfaces
      explicit rather than leaving the derived task name implicit.
```

```
[M-S-02] Identical body text across reviewer-glm.md, reviewer-kimi.md, reviewer-qwen.md
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style / Maintainability
File: .opencode/agents/reviewer-glm.md, .opencode/agents/reviewer-kimi.md, .opencode/agents/reviewer-qwen.md
Lines: 23–34 (body, all three files)
Detail: The three model-specific reviewer files differ only in their `model:` and
  `description:` frontmatter fields. The entire body text is character-for-character
  identical across all three. Any future change to reviewer instructions — adding a
  filter rule, updating a step, fixing a bug — must be applied to all three files in
  lockstep with no automated enforcement. Both Claude and GLM flagged this as out-of-scope
  for this PR but recommended a follow-up issue to track the technical debt.
Models: Claude ✓ Qwen ✗ GLM ✓
Dissenting view: Qwen did not raise this finding. Not a blocker.
Suggestion: Out-of-scope for this PR. Open a follow-up issue to investigate whether
  OpenCode supports a shared instruction file or `extends` mechanism that the three
  model-specific files could delegate to, eliminating the triplication.
```

### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

```
[S-I-01] Reviewer-family dispatch rename is unverified at runtime
Severity: Warning
Category: Testing
File: .opencode/agents/orchestrator-v3.md
Lines: 38–45, 550–555
Model: Qwen
Detail: The orchestrator now relies on OpenCode deriving task-dispatch names from filenames
  such that `reviewer-kimi.md` → "Reviewer Kimi", `reviewer-qwen.md` → "Reviewer Qwen",
  `reviewer-glm.md` → "Reviewer Glm", and `pr-reviewer.md` → "Pr Reviewer". The derivation
  pattern is plausible and consistent with the documented `test-writer.md` → "Test Writer"
  precedent. However, this PR contains no verification artifact — no smoke run, no test
  invocation, no recorded dispatch result — confirming that the exact names work in practice.
  Because the agents are pure declarative configuration, a name-resolution mismatch would
  only surface when Step 7 or `@pr-reviewer` is invoked in a live session, with no automated
  check to catch it.
Assessment: Likely genuine, though the derivation rule appears well-established. The fix-commit
  history (Claude's pre-review analysis correctly predicted the required rename, which was
  then applied) provides some indirect confidence that the naming contract is understood.
  GLM's approval without this concern suggests it may be acceptable to merge and verify at
  next use. However, Qwen's observation that no exercise of the new names has been recorded
  is factually correct and worth noting.
Suggestion: Before relying on the Step 7 review cycle, run one end-to-end dispatch of
  Reviewer Kimi, Reviewer Qwen, or Reviewer Glm and record that it succeeded (PR description
  update, or a note in `.github/notes/`). If the naming convention ever needs to support
  edge cases (abbreviations, numbers), document the derivation rule explicitly in the
  OpenCode migration plan.
```

```
[S-I-02] synthesizing-reviewer.md: {N} variable in output path not defined locally
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Documentation
File: .opencode/agents/synthesizing-reviewer.md
Lines: ~213 (Step 5)
Model: Claude
Detail: Step 5 instructs the agent to write to `.github/notes/reviews/YYYY-MM-DD-pr{N}-synthesis.md`.
  The variable `{N}` (the PR number) is not defined within the Synthesizing Reviewer's own
  file — its value arrives implicitly through the Orchestrator's Phase C dispatch prompt. An
  agent reading this instruction without the dispatch context may not know how to populate
  `{N}`. In practice this works because the Orchestrator always provides the PR number, but
  a brief parenthetical would make the contract explicit.
Assessment: Low-impact; works correctly at runtime. Minor clarity improvement.
Suggestion: Add a parenthetical after the path pattern: "...pr{N}-synthesis.md (where N is
  the PR number, provided by the Orchestrator in the dispatch prompt)."
```

## Merge Recommendation

**Approve with minor follow-up.** The blocking correctness defect (name mismatch in allow-list) was resolved before two of three reviewers ran. The post-fix structure is correct: all five agent files are well-formed, permission models are appropriate, the synthesizer correctly implements `task: deny`, and the orchestrator allow-list and Step 7 dispatch instructions are internally consistent. No Critical or blocking findings remain open. Items 2–4 above can be addressed in a follow-up commit or issue without holding this PR.
